chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn Ayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur al-Ansari was in Medina, while the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) was in Mecca. When death approached him, the Messenger of Allah and the Muslims were praying towards Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem). So Al-Bara' instructed that when he was buried, his face should be placed facing the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) towards the Qibla. He also instructed to give one-third of his wealth, and this became the established Sunnah.
Ahmad ibn Muhammad said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq wrote to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him):

That Durr, daughter of Muqatil, passed away and left a property in shares in a specific location. She bequeathed to her master from her shares an amount exceeding one-third. We are her executors, and we wished to refer this to our Master. If he ordered the bequest to be executed as it is, we would execute it; and if he ordered otherwise, we would adhere to his command in all that he commands, God willing. He (peace be upon him) wrote with his own hand: 'It is not obligatory for her in her estate except one-third. And if you give freely and are the heirs, it is permissible for you.'

key_terms.الثُّلُثِ: One-third, the standard limit for bequests
key_terms.الْبَرَاءُ بْنُ مَعْرُورٍ: Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur, a companion of the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the maximum limit for a bequest in Islamic law, and can it exceed one-third if the heir is the beneficiary?
ai.summary: This hadith establishes the foundational Shia jurisprudence regarding bequests (wasiyyah), confirming the one-third limit while distinguishing between the obligatory portion and the permissibility of exceeding it when the bequeather is also an heir. It highlights the historical precedent of Al-Bara' ibn Ma'rur’s specific instruction to face the Prophet in Mecca while buried in Medina, reflecting the transitional period before the Qibla changed to Jerusalem, and provides a practical legal ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) on the validity of bequests exceeding one-third by heirs.
